newsitem.title: JAMAICA: First women priests ordained in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: First women priests ordained in Caribbean.

text.p: Four women have been ordained as priests in Jamaica, the first in the 330-year history of the Anglican church in the Caribbean.

Rev. Howard Spence, who delivered the main sermon at the ceremony in Spanish Town, near Kingston, on Sunday said the four were part of a "movement to a new frontier" for the West Indian province of the Anglican church.
The four were Sybil Morris, Vivette Jennings, Judith Daniel and Patricia Johnson. They also created history two years ago when they became the first women to be ordained as deacons.
The Caribbean churches have been discussing the ordination of women since the 1970s. Final approval was given last year.

The topic remains controversial as several male priests in the Anglican church in Britain, to which the West Indian province is affiliated, left the ranks when women were first ordained there two years ago.
It has also remained a major doctrinal difference in reunification talks between the Anglican and Roman Catholic churches.
